headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Airbyte can egress business data while pdf.js processes PDFs, creating a default path for sensitive document content to flow into downstream outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not default. However, Airbyte can move file-derived content through APIs and pdf.js processes PDF files in a browser-based worker, so a manual copy/paste or file handoff path exists. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, making low-severity injection plausible but not dominant.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airbyte-produced text into pdf.js inputs or browser tests
IF pdf.js consumes untrusted PDF text as instructions in a downstream workflow
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Use a strict copy/paste policy for any text moved between them
Strip instructions from extracted text before reuse
Add a provenance note to every transferred artifact

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and touches business data, while pdf.js handles PDF files and has no network egress. If they share a workspace or file handoff, document contents can flow from Airbyte-managed data into pdf.js processing and then into outputs. The pathway is plausible in default operational use, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data into files later opened by pdf.js
IF the two agents share a workspace or mounted volume
mitigations: Separate storage locations for each agent
Disable automatic export of business data into PDFs
Review any PDF inputs before opening them in pdf.js
Use least-privilege file permissions
Log every cross-agent file transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has API access and broad egress, while pdf.js is browser-based with no network egress and supports multiple instances. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource contention is limited. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or shared mutable resource not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable resource
IF Airbyte API actions and pdf.js file operations target the same directory
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize any shared-resource operations
Avoid concurrent writes to the same files
Use per-agent service accounts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data, and pdf.js can render or process PDFs that may be treated as authoritative downstream. If Airbyte output is fed into pdf.js without verification, errors or malformed content can cascade into user-visible documents. The profiles do not show a verification step, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is used as source material for pdf.js rendering
IF no human or automated verification occurs before pdf.js consumes the output
mitigations: Add a validation step before PDF generation or rendering
Compare extracted values against source records
Require human review for high-impact documents
Reject malformed or incomplete records early

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress, while pdf.js processes PDF documents locally with no network egress. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling gaps rather than a documented breach path. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF business data includes regulated content
IF PDFs generated from Airbyte data are stored or transmitted outside approved controls
mitigations: Classify the data before transfer
Keep regulated PDFs in approved storage only
Set retention rules for exported documents
Review access logs weekly
